purpose: Deterministic synthetic athlete fixtures and machine-readable release-gate rules for LetMeFly behavioral, persistence, unit, coaching, substitution, safety, and program-integrity audits.

profile.primaryGoal: build foundational strength and work capacity

requiredAssertions: light percentage prescriptions remain sensible
near-empty-bar loads render without impossible plate math
only available plates are prescribed by the Bar Loader
beginner coaching does not rewrite the program
progression is not inflated merely because absolute loads are small
end-to-end normal workflow passes
prescription and circuit order match the program snapshot
logging, resume, completion, history, progress, and Coach agree on the same athlete state
a core failure is treated as an application-level regression until disproven

profile.primaryGoal: maximize strength while preserving athletic capacity

requiredAssertions: heavy multi-plate loading is accurate
large load, volume, e1RM, and PR values remain readable
desktop Home, Train, Program, Progress, and Coach remain usable
high values do not overflow, truncate, or corrupt calculations
training maxes remain kilograms internally and visually
Bar Loader uses a 20 kg bar and metric plate inventory
logged loads, history, progress, PRs, Coach, export, and restore preserve kilograms
no hidden pound assumption changes the meaning of a value

profile.primaryGoal: continue productive training while managing fatigue

readiness.notes: Synthetic poor-readiness audit seed. Not a medical condition.

requiredAssertions: poor readiness is saved and visible to Coach
adjustments remain within program-defined boundaries
one poor day does not permanently reduce training maxes
one poor day does not rewrite future program structure
original prescription remains identifiable when execution is adjusted
the next workout remains intact

profile.primaryGoal: continue productive training while respecting a reported lower-body limitation

scenarios.label: reported-hip-limitation
scenarios.reportedLimitation: Reports anterior hip pinching/discomfort during deep hip flexion, especially deep squats. Avoid provocative ranges today. LetMeFly is not making a diagnosis.
requiredMovementCoverage: lower-body movement that may remain tolerable such as hinge, carry, or sled work
requiredAssertions: do not blindly replace one deep squat with another deep squat
consider movement pattern, intended stimulus, tolerable range, equipment, phase, and skill
preserve the canonical programmed exercise
record prescribed and performed exercise identities
populate substituted_from_exercise_key when a substitution is used
explain why the substitute fits
Coach can later explain why the substitution was used

scenarios.label: reported-knee-limitation
scenarios.reportedLimitation: Reports knee pain aggravated by loaded or deep knee flexion. Avoid provocative range/loading today. LetMeFly is not making a diagnosis.
requiredMovementCoverage: alternative that preserves purpose without reproducing the stated trigger
requiredAssertions: recommendations materially account for the knee trigger rather than reusing generic lower-body substitutions
preserve the original program exercise and future workouts
record prescribed and performed exercise identities
populate substituted_from_exercise_key when a substitution is used
Coach does not diagnose the source of pain

scenarios.label: safety-escalation
requiredAssertions: Coach stops treating the situation as a routine substitution problem
Coach recommends appropriate professional evaluation
Coach does not diagnose the condition
Coach does not encourage training through a red-flag presentation

universalAuditFlow.assert: Reset the selected athlete to the locked fixture and confirm identity, units, barbell inventory, TMs, readiness/limitation state, program instance, week, and day.
Profile values render correctly and any changes remain scoped to the current athlete.
Current program, week/day, today's workout, recent performance, and next milestone agree with athlete state.
Exercise order, sets, reps, load rules, circuit/superset grouping, notes, phase, and week/day match the canonical program snapshot.
Readiness saves correctly and affects execution only within supported autoregulation boundaries.
Workout instructions and grouping are correct and previous/current performance belongs to the current athlete.
Total weight, bar weight, unit, and plates per side are valid for the athlete's plate inventory.
Reps, load, RPE/RIR, tempo where present, rest state, notes, and completion persist correctly.
Refresh/reopen resumes the correct athlete and workout without losing or duplicating saved sets.
When applicable, substitution preserves training purpose, records provenance, respects limitations/equipment/phase, and does not mutate the source program.
Workout completes once, creates correct history, and advances program state only according to program rules.
History contains correct prescribed/performed exercise data, loads, units, RPE/RIR, notes, and substitution provenance.
Volume, e1RM, PRs, completion, and other applicable metrics are athlete-scoped and unit-correct.
Coach uses athlete profile, program phase, current workout, history, readiness, and limitations without inventing program changes or diagnoses.
Backup/export and restore preserve athlete identity, units, TMs, program state, workout history, and relationships.
A second QA athlete shows none of the state created for the athlete just audited.
Canonical program definition/snapshot before and after the run is unchanged unless the test explicitly exercises an authorized governed program edit.

dataIntegrityAssertions: athlete IDs are stable and unique
workout sessions, exercises, and sets reference the correct athlete_id
substituted_from_exercise_key is populated for performed substitutions
performed substitutions do not permanently replace canonical program exercises
workoutSets.load_unit and TM units match athlete settings
refresh/retry does not duplicate completion or history records
backup/restore preserves athlete identity and relational integrity
synthetic QA fixtures cannot overwrite a real athlete record
majorDefectExamples: supported desktop or mobile workflow failure
Coach ignores available athlete context without creating an immediate safety risk
minorDefectExamples: copy issue that does not obscure prescriptions, controls, units, safety information, or logged values
